items.headline: PW Spotlight: Time to Reclaim the Driver's Seat in AI
items.excerpt: Bookpact.ai, founded by Sander Ruys, is a licensing platform that lets publishers set per-deal terms, compensation and usage tracking for how AI companies access their titles. (Marked Sponsored / PW Studio content.)

items.headline: The Cost of Deepfakes: PW Talks with Meena Kandasamy
items.excerpt: In the novelist's 'Fieldwork as a Sex Object' (Soft Skull, Nov.), a young Indian woman faces harassment after someone posts a deepfake video of her. Kandasamy discusses writing fiction about synthetic media harm.

items.headline: Ask the Chefs: AI and Copyright Licensing
items.excerpt: The US Department of Justice filed a Statement of Interest in the NYT v. OpenAI/Microsoft copyright litigation, largely siding with the AI companies and favoring LLM training as fair use. A panel of publishing experts reacts to what it means for content licensing.

items.headline: The Evolving World of Literary Rights: Moving Beyond the Printed Page
items.excerpt: An essay on how literary rights have stretched from print to screens, games and now AI systems, and what that means for how authors and agents negotiate deals today.

items.headline: Flowtica Verso is an e-Ink AI screen that attaches to your phone
items.excerpt: The Flowtica Verso's always-on e-paper display sets it apart from standard screenless AI voice recorders, pairing ambient AI capture with an E-Ink reading surface.
